key_insight: Adding multilayer compositional gradients to plasma-sprayed LZO/NiCoCrAlY coatings smooths the ceramic-to-metal transition, reducing stress concentration and improving high-temperature durability.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical route to extend thermal barrier coating life in gas turbines and other extreme-temperature systems by mitigating thermal mismatch damage.
method: Built double-layer, three-layer, and five-layer LZO/NAY gradient thermal barrier coatings by plasma spraying.
Characterized microstructure and interfaces using SEM, EBSD, and TEM.
Used finite element modeling plus thermal shock and oxidation tests to assess stress, insulation, and durability.
evidence_signal: The five-layer gradient coating showed the most uniform stress distribution, survived 24 thermal shock cycles at 1200 °C, and formed thinner thermally grown oxide layers than the conventional system.
watch_item: Greater layer complexity can improve performance, but it may also increase process control demands and manufacturing sensitivity in scale-up.
paper_title: Multilayer Gradient Design for Stress Mitigation and Durability Enhancement in Plasma-Sprayed La₂Zr₂O₇/NiCoCrAlY Coatings
